# Geographic and occupancy completion — September 13, 2026

**Decision ID:** GEO-COMPLETE-20260913  
**Authority:** repository owner’s explicit delegation, recorded in [the authorization](../../geospatial/finalization/AUTHORIZATION.md).  
**Integration boundary:** these decisions become controlling with acceptance of this addendum into main. A proposal checkout remains pending.  
**Scope:** geographic representation, fictional accommodation, source-disposition and temporal precision. No business redesign, financial approval, real property conveyance, signature, procurement execution or operational control certification.

## Continuity and decision method

Read this addendum with the existing [corporate headquarters doctrine](CORPORATE_HEADQUARTERS_CLOSEOUT_2026-09-03.md), [Willow closeout](WILLOW_KLEIN_CLOSEOUT_2026-09-06.md), [approved Klein/Fort history](KLEIN_FORT_OCCUPANCY_2026-09-13.md), [Cradle closeout](CRADLE_CLOSEOUT_2026-09-06.md), [J2 Education doctrine](../j2/EDUCATION.md), [corporate lore](SABLE_HARBOR_CORPORATE_LORE_CANON_v0.3.1.md), and [runtime hosting decisions](RUNTIME_HOSTING_AND_DATA_CENTER_DECISIONS_2026-09-11.md). Their institutional roles, operating limitations, ownership distinctions and accepted dates continue to control.

This is a limited successor to the geographic uncertainties in those sources. It does not replace their narratives or turn every earlier provisional number into canon. In particular, the proposed office populations in the [2026 operating model](../finance/SABLE_HARBOR_CORPORATE_FUNDAMENTALS_AND_2026_OPERATING_MODEL_v0.1.md) remain model inputs. Exact room capacities and local-frame layouts remain engineering representations unless independently accepted.

The master execution handover is preserved as a historical mandate. Later accepted canon controls Bedford/Fairmont over Belle/Kanawha, Willow/Klein over former name assumptions, Taylor over obsolete Bloodstone naming, and Red Wash’s truck/product/custody boundaries over early speculative railway concepts.

## Current accommodation decisions

The following are deliberately authored fictional decisions under the owner’s delegation, reconciled to the sources above. They are not claims that an executed lease or real-world occupancy record was discovered.

| Object | Controlling accommodation decision | Temporal and precision treatment |
|---|---|---|
| SH-SITE-0001 — Sacramento headquarters | Preserve the Railyards / River District setting and the approved architectural source and local campus frame. The geographic envelope is a fictional planning footprint, with real roads and facilities retained as reference. | Occupied headquarters is supported by the September 3 closeout. Earlier entry and construction dates remain unknown; incorporation in 2016 is not a campus opening date. |
| SH-SITE-0002 — Klein shop | Retain the leased historical Pittsburgh-area industrial shop as a distinct predecessor premise. | The 2021 lease narrative, continued use after recharter and 2024 vacation control. Exact historical building/address and lease days remain intentionally unspecified; no current site is relabeled as the old shop. |
| SH-SITE-0003 — the Fort | Separate Pittsburgh/Hazelwood industrial premises retain the Big Shed, Small Shed with temporary lodging, White Shed, and outdoor Museum. | The accepted staged 2024 entry controls. Each component belongs to the Fort; independent commissioning dates are unknown rather than automatically copied from the parent. |
| SH-SITE-0004 — Emberline | Charleston remains the field/commercial program’s historical center. Successor functions receive its work and records; a continuing independent Emberline campus is not established. | 2022–2025 describes the venture, not a universal property lease. Lease-exit days and individual premises remain unknown. |
| SH-SITE-0005 — Bedford | Preserve a 15–20-acre fictional redeveloped industrial brownfield in the Fairmont area, distinct from Demotte and the Fort. Road-based receipt and outbound service support the accepted development/upgrading role. No berth, dedicated railway siding, in-house individual-element separation or magnet production is added. | The September 6 early-commercial operating snapshot controls. Earlier first occupancy and cleanup-completion dates are unknown; the site-selection decision does not impersonate an environmental clearance. |
| SH-SITE-0011 — Reno office | Adopt shared leased office/engineering accommodation in the Reno urban area for Foundry and associated delivery work. It is an office, distinct from the selected Tahoe-Reno colocation provider and owned data-center program. | Newly established fictional current accommodation at the September 13 snapshot. Exact suite, address and commencement day are intentionally unspecified. No proposed headcount is ratified. |
| SH-SITE-0012 — Elko field office | Adopt a modest shared field base for mine-customer work, equipment staging and temporary project attendance. It is not a new campus or a claim on a customer mine. | September 13 current fictional accommodation; historical lease/entry dates unknown. City-level public precision. |
| SH-SITE-0013 — Tucson office | Adopt shared leased engineering/analysis accommodation for the existing geology, mining science and Atlas Meridian seam. Preserve operator and business decision rights. | September 13 current fictional accommodation; exact suite and historic entry dates unknown. The planning model’s office population remains unapproved. |
| SH-SITE-0014 — J2 Education | A distinct residential learning campus and conference center in the Sacramento metropolitan region, organizationally part of J2 and physically separate from the headquarters office floor. It supports the accepted classrooms, case rooms, simulated executive/board settings, residential attendance and convening mission. | Current institution under the September 3 J2 decision. Regional siting is sufficient for this edition; a particular real school, hotel or conference property is not selected. Exact address, property interests and entry date remain explicitly unknown. This is not reduced to distributed meeting rooms. |
| SH-SITE-0015 — J2 headquarters | Dedicated controlled institutional accommodation within the Sacramento corporate headquarters, with J2’s protected reporting/access boundary preserved. Physical co-location does not place J2 inside ESS. | Parent-site relationship; not an additional owned campus or duplicate real-estate asset. Separate fit-out/entry date unknown. |
| SH-SITE-0017 — Foundry / Foundry Field | Shared Reno/Sacramento accommodation plus customer-embedded and mobile field work; no independent corporate campus is created. | Use the shared sites’ precision. Customer attendance is neither customer-property ownership nor permanent tenancy. |
| SH-SITE-0018 — Atlas Meridian | Shared Tucson/Sacramento accommodation and deployed work through existing business interfaces; no separate owned campus. | Functional accommodation relationship rather than a duplicate parcel. |
| SH-SITE-0019 — Advisory | Shared headquarters/project accommodation and customer engagements. Project hubs do not automatically create permanent offices. | Individual unrecorded engagement premises remain unknown and are not separately fabricated. |
| SH-SITE-0026 — earlier headquarters/offices | Preserve Sacramento as the incorporation and working-headquarters location from 2016. Earlier accommodation remains a historical collection, distinct from the current campus. | No invented sequence of street addresses, leases or disposal dates. Member premises are not collectively assigned one polygon or occupancy interval. |

## Selected geographic implementation

The controlling design coordinates are the three features in [SITE_SELECTIONS.geojson](../../geospatial/finalization/SITE_SELECTIONS.geojson), with reproducible measurements and reference checks in [SITE_SCREEN.json](../../geospatial/finalization/SITE_SCREEN.json). They are deliberately authored fictional footprints. Coordinate precision describes the design, not survey accuracy, a cadastral tax lot, real land availability or an executed property instrument.

**Sacramento headquarters — SH-SITE-0001.** Select the 11.57-acre Railyards footprint north of Railyards Boulevard, east of Fifth Street and west of Seventh Street. Preserve the 840 × 600 ft local campus envelope and the approved exterior image. The geographic placement avoids the archived railway centerline and visible surrounding buildings; the reference terrain requires ordinary redevelopment/grading interpretation, not an assertion that the whole campus is already level in aerial photographs. The city’s Railyards planning context and stadium project remain external reference; neither the stadium nor a state office becomes headquarters. Arrival connects conceptually to the surrounding street network, with public streets and transit retained outside company ownership.

**The Fort — SH-SITE-0003.** Select the 10.65-acre elongated former-industrial planning footprint north of the real Roundhouse, between the Blair Street side of the redevelopment and the retained eastern road-reference exclusion. This places the fictional campus in Hazelwood rather than across the Monongahela River on a wooded hillside. Its three modest sheds and outdoor Museum form a connected industrial compound along the long axis. Preserve the Big Shed’s research role, Small Shed’s administration and temporary lodging, White Shed’s controlled intake/storage, and Museum’s outdoor working collection. The older 250 × 243 m local-frame plan is a program illustration, not a georeferenced as-built plan; its room capacities and building dimensions do not become actual occupancy evidence. The new geographic arrangement does not redesign the approved identities or erase that earlier illustrative plan.

The real Roundhouse, Mill 19, CMU Robotics Innovation Center, Pitt BioForge, community field, parks, roads and railroad remain external neighbors. The selected footprint excludes their identified developed/planned areas. Retain a twelve-meter minimum exclusion from the archived ordinary-road centerlines; this is an analyst design clearance, not a claim that a legal right-of-way is exactly that width. The screened footprint includes a mapped 0.2% annual-chance flood-hazard portion. Keep drainage, emergency access and experimental containment as explicit design constraints; do not describe the property as flood-proof. The already accepted staged 2024 move applies to the fictional Fort; no real Hazelwood developer or tenant is asserted to have executed that transaction.

**Bedford — SH-SITE-0005.** Select the 15.27-acre Fairmont/White Hall-area redevelopment footprint. The in-world predecessor is an unnamed industrial works yard reclaimed for Bedford’s research, development, assembly and intermediate upgrading; that previous use is expressly authored fiction, not a discovered history of a real tax parcel. Place the working buildings and handling areas on the upper redevelopment bench. Retain the steep outer ground as a landscape/drainage buffer, not a flat process floor or spare building pad. The approximately 44 m total sampled relief is a property-wide terrain range, not an acceptable building-floor slope. Keep surrounding occupied buildings and public roads outside the footprint. Road receipt and dispatch use the local service-road setting; no public-road access authorization, rail siding, river berth, cleanup certificate or additional process capability is implied.

Bedford is not the actual Fairmont Coke Works Superfund site, the city’s Helmick/Box Factory cleanup projects, a NASA facility, a shopping-center tenant, or Demotte. Its fictional brownfield history cannot establish completion of any real remediation obligation. Site rights, contamination characterization, utility capacity, finished grading and statutory approvals belong to actual external execution if anyone ever proposes real development; this canon decision does not execute it.

The original nine linework-screened alternatives remain archived and are rejected for final placement: imagery and elevation disclose occupied infrastructure, unsuitable terrain, or both. Their historical publication is preserved as a record of alternatives, not silently rewritten as accepted siting.

### Real-geography reference basis

The [retained reference manifest](../../geospatial/finalization/reference/MANIFEST.json) binds exact federal data bytes, request URLs, acquisition metadata and hashes. The USGS NAIP catalog identifies 2022 acquisitions at the candidate query points. These are not September 2026 aerial observations. USGS 3DEP supplies sampled terrain; FEMA NFHL supplies mapped flood-zone intersections. None supplies title, tenancy, contamination clearance or engineering certification.

Current-context checks also use the [City of Sacramento Railyards project](https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/major-projects/railyards-project) and [2025 stadium environmental addendum](https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/content/dam/portal/cdd/Planning/Environmental-Impact-Reports/sac-republic-fc-stadium-%28z25-042%29/Sac%20Republic%20FC%20Stadium%20%28Z25-042%29%20Addendum.pdf); [Hazelwood Green’s current site occupants](https://hazelwoodgreen.com/whats-here/) and [January 2025 city planning presentation, page 2](https://www.pittsburghpa.gov/files/assets/city/v/1/dcp/documents/planning-commission/01-28-2025-meeting/bda-2024-05483-lytle-st-multi-unit-presentation-2025-01-28.pdf); [CMU’s Robotics Innovation Center project](https://www.cmu.edu/cdfd/buildings/ric/index.html); [Fairmont’s named municipal cleanup projects](https://fairmontwv.gov/502/Former-Helmick-Property-and-Box-Factory-); and [EPA’s Fairmont Coke Works record](https://cumulis.epa.gov/supercpad/cursites/csitinfo.cfm?id=0302883). They constrain the fiction and identify excluded real facilities. They do not certify that any selected fictional site is commercially available.

## External hosts, reference geography and historical cases

Blackridge remains the Nevada open-pit copper-and-gold operation associated with Argent Ridge Mining and the 2015 antecedent catastrophe. It is not retrospectively acquired by Sable Harbor. The operational dataset’s local pit/bench/facility identities remain valid within their model; an exact real Nevada mine is not appropriated to manufacture a geographic answer. Regional geographic precision and unknown exact siting are deliberate, accepted dispositions for this historical case.

The Forty-Seven Names customer operation remains a distinct Nevada copper-operation case. Its 2016 incident date is not a tenancy or acquisition date. Glasshouse remains an underground machine-vision trial whose failure in real mine conditions informs Willow; it does not create a Sable Harbor-owned underground mine. Wallaby remains a rejected residue/tailings opportunity, not an operating Cradle asset. Exact anonymized customer locations and trial/lease days add no necessary geographic truth and remain explicitly unknown.

Kelly Gang Mining / Stream 17 remains an external Tasmanian host. Demotte Reclamation Services remains a separate external north-central West Virginia AMD treatment host with the accepted operating U.S. Gen 1 deployment. Their process/recovery interfaces may be represented with local engineering geometry. Neither host is Bedford, neither host’s plant or mine is transferred to Cradle, and neither a process-flow drawing nor equipment presence creates title or environmental authority. Regional host geography and unknown exact host parcels remain accepted public precision.

The licensed conversion destination is an external, independently custody-gated delivery dependency. Exact licensed recipient, destination and execution evidence remain in that operating workflow. Geographic closeout records the boundary rather than inventing a recipient or release authorization.

ARU’s terminal/warehouse/trucking estate and customer interfaces are collections of individually represented facilities and relationships. The mapped industrial members remain controlling. No extra aggregate parcel, uniform acquisition date or blanket ownership of customer interfaces is created.

## Runtime estate boundary

SH-SITE-0016 and SH-SITE-0028 through SH-SITE-0030 retain the September 11 runtime source states: selected Switch Tahoe-Reno primary transition, selected IDACORE Boise independent recovery, and the fictional Northern Nevada acquired-land/preconstruction program. Provider selection does not become executed procurement or operation. No occupied building, installed capacity or accepted control test is manufactured by this geographic addendum. Their outstanding external-execution requirements remain with the runtime workflow.

## Time and historical representation

Preserve the existing 73 source-bound events and the accepted effective intervals of the engineered railway network. Historical institutional events, acquisitions, field incidents and site occupancy are separate predicates. A current route is not projected into an earlier year merely because its corporate predecessor already existed. Unsourced early and abandoned alignments remain explicitly unlocated history, with their source claims retained.

An unknown day is stored as null with its reason; a supported year is represented as a bounded interval; a dated current observation is represented as a snapshot, not a fabricated opening. Shared functions, component records and collections use relationships rather than duplicate tenancies. Recording the current decision date does not overwrite the in-world dates of older facts.

## Acceptance of bounded uncertainty

The owner expressly authorized unknown or not-applicable dispositions where precision adds no value. The specific historical addresses, anonymized trial/host parcels, non-property collections and independently gated runtime/custody facts identified above are such dispositions. They are not hidden work queues or assertions that missing documents exist.

This acceptance does not waive geographic review or engineering. Every source and discovered claim must still have a traceable disposition; selected geometry must retain its construction and real-context screening; rendered products must consume the governed data; and release/QGIS/browser/temporal validation must pass before the associated implementation issue closes. Newly discovered material contradictions require reconciliation under existing canon rather than automatic dismissal as immaterial.

**Bedford — SH-SITE-0005.** Select the 15.27-acre Fairmont/White Hall-area redevelopment footprint. The in-world predecessor is an unnamed industrial works yard reclaimed for Bedford’s research, development, assembly and intermediate upgrading; that previous use is expressly authored fiction, not a discovered history of a real tax parcel. Place the working buildings and handling areas on the upper redevelopment bench. Retain the steep outer ground as a landscape/drainage buffer, not a flat process floor or spare building pad. The approximately 44 m total sampled relief is a property-wide terrain range, not an acceptable building-floor slope. Keep surrounding occupied buildings and public roads outside the footprint. Road receipt and dispatch use the local service-road setting; no public-road access authorization, rail siding, river berth, cleanup certificate or additional process capability is implied.

Bedford is not the actual Fairmont Coke Works Superfund site, the city’s Helmick/Box Factory cleanup projects, a NASA facility, a shopping-center tenant, or Demotte. Its fictional brownfield history cannot establish completion of any real remediation obligation. Site rights, contamination characterization, utility capacity, finished grading and statutory approvals belong to actual external execution if anyone ever proposes real development; this canon decision does not execute it.

The original nine linework-screened alternatives remain archived and are rejected for final placement: imagery and elevation disclose occupied infrastructure, unsuitable terrain, or both. Their historical publication is preserved as a record of alternatives, not silently rewritten as accepted siting.

### Real-geography reference basis

The [retained reference manifest](../../geospatial/finalization/reference/MANIFEST.json) binds exact federal data bytes, request URLs, acquisition metadata and hashes. The USGS NAIP catalog identifies 2022 acquisitions at the candidate query points. These are not September 2026 aerial observations. USGS 3DEP supplies sampled terrain; FEMA NFHL supplies mapped flood-zone intersections. None supplies title, tenancy, contamination clearance or engineering certification.

Current-context checks also use the [City of Sacramento Railyards project](https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/major-projects/railyards-project) and [2025 stadium environmental addendum](https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/content/dam/portal/cdd/Planning/Environmental-Impact-Reports/sac-republic-fc-stadium-%28z25-042%29/Sac%20Republic%20FC%20Stadium%20%28Z25-042%29%20Addendum.pdf); [Hazelwood Green’s current site occupants](https://hazelwoodgreen.com/whats-here/) and [January 2025 city planning presentation, page 2](https://www.pittsburghpa.gov/files/assets/city/v/1/dcp/documents/planning-commission/01-28-2025-meeting/bda-2024-05483-lytle-st-multi-unit-presentation-2025-01-28.pdf); [CMU’s Robotics Innovation Center project](https://www.cmu.edu/cdfd/buildings/ric/index.html); [Fairmont’s named municipal cleanup projects](https://fairmontwv.gov/502/Former-Helmick-Property-and-Box-Factory-); and [EPA’s Fairmont Coke Works record](https://cumulis.epa.gov/supercpad/cursites/csitinfo.cfm?id=0302883). They constrain the fiction and identify excluded real facilities. They do not certify that any selected fictional site is commercially available.

## External hosts, reference geography and historical cases

Blackridge remains the Nevada open-pit copper-and-gold operation associated with Argent Ridge Mining and the 2015 antecedent catastrophe. It is not retrospectively acquired by Sable Harbor. The operational dataset’s local pit/bench/facility identities remain valid within their model; an exact real Nevada mine is not appropriated to manufacture a geographic answer. Regional geographic precision and unknown exact siting are deliberate, accepted dispositions for this historical case.

The Forty-Seven Names customer operation remains a distinct Nevada copper-operation case. Its 2016 incident date is not a tenancy or acquisition date. Glasshouse remains an underground machine-vision trial whose failure in real mine conditions informs Willow; it does not create a Sable Harbor-owned underground mine. Wallaby remains a rejected residue/tailings opportunity, not an operating Cradle asset. Exact anonymized customer locations and trial/lease days add no necessary geographic truth and remain explicitly unknown.

Kelly Gang Mining / Stream 17 remains an external Tasmanian host. Demotte Reclamation Services remains a separate external north-central West Virginia AMD treatment host with the accepted operating U.S. Gen 1 deployment. Their process/recovery interfaces may be represented with local engineering geometry. Neither host is Bedford, neither host’s plant or mine is transferred to Cradle, and neither a process-flow drawing nor equipment presence creates title or environmental authority. Regional host geography and unknown exact host parcels remain accepted public precision.

The licensed conversion destination is an external, independently custody-gated delivery dependency. Exact licensed recipient, destination and execution evidence remain in that operating workflow. Geographic closeout records the boundary rather than inventing a recipient or release authorization.

ARU’s terminal/warehouse/trucking estate and customer interfaces are collections of individually represented facilities and relationships. The mapped industrial members remain controlling. No extra aggregate parcel, uniform acquisition date or blanket ownership of customer interfaces is created.

## Runtime estate boundary

SH-SITE-0016 and SH-SITE-0028 through SH-SITE-0030 retain the September 11 runtime source states: selected Switch Tahoe-Reno primary transition, selected IDACORE Boise independent recovery, and the fictional Northern Nevada acquired-land/preconstruction program. Provider selection does not become executed procurement or operation. No occupied building, installed capacity or accepted control test is manufactured by this geographic addendum. Their outstanding external-execution requirements remain with the runtime workflow.

## Time and historical representation

Preserve the existing 73 source-bound events and the accepted effective intervals of the engineered railway network. Historical institutional events, acquisitions, field incidents and site occupancy are separate predicates. A current route is not projected into an earlier year merely because its corporate predecessor already existed. Unsourced early and abandoned alignments remain explicitly unlocated history, with their source claims retained.

An unknown day is stored as null with its reason; a supported year is represented as a bounded interval; a dated current observation is represented as a snapshot, not a fabricated opening. Shared functions, component records and collections use relationships rather than duplicate tenancies. Recording the current decision date does not overwrite the in-world dates of older facts.

## Acceptance of bounded uncertainty

The owner expressly authorized unknown or not-applicable dispositions where precision adds no value. The specific historical addresses, anonymized trial/host parcels, non-property collections and independently gated runtime/custody facts identified above are such dispositions. They are not hidden work queues or assertions that missing documents exist.

This acceptance does not waive geographic review or engineering. Every source and discovered claim must still have a traceable disposition; selected geometry must retain its construction and real-context screening; rendered products must consume the governed data; and release/QGIS/browser/temporal validation must pass before the associated implementation issue closes. Newly discovered material contradictions require reconciliation under existing canon rather than automatic dismissal as immaterial.

Willow's Pittsburgh-area physical center is a roughly **10–20 acre** industrial compound informally and then routinely called **the Fort**. The Fort is a working industrial research site, not a landscaped corporate campus.

The site has three principal structures:

1. **The Big Shed** — Willow's main research building and laboratory. Most experimental work, instrumentation, prototyping, integration, bench work, and hands-on research occurs here. It is explicitly not the primary administrative building and not bulk storage.
2. **The Small Shed** — administrative offices plus a small attached lodging component, effectively a modest internal mini-hotel for temporary stays by visiting staff, collaborators, field personnel, or employees whose work requires them to remain at the Fort for short periods. It is not permanent employee housing.
3. **The White Shed** — controlled intake, secure storage, utility, mechanical, staging, and quarantine space for unusual equipment, samples, field gear, or material that should not move directly onto the Big Shed research floor.

The remaining grounds are intentionally spare: controlled perimeter and gate, gravel circulation, hardstand, outdoor staging, utility/service areas, and practical non-sensitive storage. The working yards and accumulated outdoor collection are collectively known as **the Museum**. The name is affectionate and literal enough to persist: obsolete rigs, retired prototypes, industrial fragments, and odd pieces of equipment can remain because they preserve useful physical history, not because Willow is operating a public museum.
